workflowRecommendation: One implementer, one pull request (spec: nothing here is independently shippable). Work the steps in order; steps 1 and 2 (client + error class) are independent of each other and both precede step 4. Write each step's tests first against the fake client and the manual clock, then the code. Do not run the whole repo suite between steps; run `bun test packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/worker-rpc.test.ts`, then `processes.test.ts`, then `index.test.ts`, then the new real-tmux e2e; finish with `cd packages/daemon && bun test`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bunx biome check src/`.
summary: Delivery of a prompt to a live phase worker currently means `client.prompt()` resolved, i.e. the shim's `{success:true}` acknowledgement. OMP answers that acknowledgement before it starts the turn (`packages/coding-agent/src/modes/rpc/rpc-mode.ts` `case "prompt"`: `session.prompt(...)` is started, not awaited, then `return success(id, "prompt")`), and a fork build since commit 0e57a6ca can accept a message that starts no turn. This plan makes delivery mean an observed turn start: the `WorkerRpcClient` returns a receipt whose `turnStarted` promise settles on the first `agent_start` frame (or a `get_state` answer with `isStreaming: true`) seen after the prompt was written; `ProcessManager.promptExistingWorker` races that receipt against `boundedWait(workerRpcTimeoutMs, deps.sleep)` (the same injectable clock `awaitShutdown` uses) and commits the delivery bookkeeping — `phases[issue]` for an assignment, `pendingAssignment` cleared, `promptFailures` reset, queue entry removed, persist — only on a started turn. No turn within the bound throws `PromptNotStarted`, which every one of the three prompt sites handles as a prompt failure with the existing count/retry/retire accounting, and a turn that starts after the bound is committed by a continuation on the same receipt, never re-prompted. No state schema change, no daemon API contract change.
verifiedFacts: `WorkerRpcClient.prompt()` (packages/daemon/src/daemon/worker-rpc.ts:367-385) sets `runState = "running"` before writing the request and restores it only on a `{success:false}` rejection; `handleLine` (295-299) sets `running` on `agent_start` and calls `markIdle()` on `agent_end`; `getState()` (386-403) seeds `runState` from `data.isStreaming`. There is no per-prompt turn-start signal today.

OMP rpc-mode replies to `prompt` immediately (`return success(id, "prompt")` after starting `session.prompt` without awaiting it) and, when the prompt starts no agent turn, later emits `{type:"prompt_result", id, agentInvoked:false}`; when the worker is already streaming, `session.prompt` throws `AgentBusyError`, which surfaces as a late `{type:"response", success:false}` for the same id — our client ignores it because the id already settled on the first (success) response. Both facts hold at the pinned fork build `v18.1.18-sami.20260912-104423` (dec271b09911 contains 0e57a6ca).

`ProcessManager.promptExistingWorker` (processes.ts:725-762) is the only production caller of `client.prompt()`; its three callers are `WorkerAdmission.promoteQueuedWorker`'s `"prompt"` decision (worker-admission.ts:584-640), `WorkerAdmission.resumeOrQueueExisting`'s admitted branch (364-400, reached from `ProcessManager.deliverToWorker` at processes.ts:653), and `ProcessManager.workerReady` (processes.ts:786-884, line 861). All three run inside `workerAdmission.mutateClaim(token)`.

`/legion/v1/worker/ready` (api/routes/workers.ts:330-351) responds before calling `processManager.workerReady(...)` detached, so a bounded wait inside `workerReady` never delays the worker's boot handshake and a throw there is only logged — the not-started outcome must be handled inside `workerReady` itself.

In the direct `resumed` path (`resumeOrQueueExisting` admitted branch) `pendingAssignment` is never written to the claim before the prompt, so today a failed prompt there loses the task; the not-started handling must write it (`enqueueIdleWorker`) and queue the token.

Boot redrive for acceptance 4 already exists: `startDaemonLocked` (index.ts:553-557) awaits `reconnectWorkers()`, whose `probeWorker` `get_state` seeds an idle worker's client `runState` (processes.ts:988-1000; `markIdle` fires `onIdle` -> `promoteWorkerQueue`, gated off during the launch hold), then after `enableLaunches()` calls `reconcileWorkerAdmission()` (index.ts:701), whose `promoteQueuedWorker` prompts a queue head whose claim has a locator, `sessionId`, `readyConfirmedAt`, `pendingAssignment`, and a cached idle client (worker-admission.ts:525-565). No new code is needed for acceptance 4; the plan pins it with an `index.test.ts` case (step 7). The existing boot test at index.test.ts:443 covers only the locator-less cold-launch redrive.

The periodic linger sweep runs `reconcileWorkerAdmission()` every 60 s (index.ts:722-742, `LINGER_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`), so a not-started prompt left queued is retried within a minute even with no other trigger.

`launchWorker`'s `freshClaim` (processes.ts:2818-2839) does not carry `promptFailures`, so a worker relaunched cold after retirement starts the counter at 0; `markWorkerDeadLocked` leaves `pendingAssignment` in place and carries `ompSessionFile` into `resumeSessionFile`, so the retire-at-threshold path already falls through to a `--resume` relaunch (covered by the existing test at processes.test.ts:11555).
`legion state` reads the redacted API (`api/state.ts`), which exposes neither `workerAdmission.queue` nor `promptFailures`; the rig proof reads `<state_dir>/state.json` directly (index.ts:316).

clientContract.interface: export interface PromptReceipt { /** Resolves when the worker's turn is observed to start: the first `agent_start` frame, or a `get_state` answer with `isStreaming: true`, seen on this connection after this prompt was written. Never rejects and never times out — the caller bounds it — and still resolves after `abandonWait()` (a late start). Settled at most once. */ readonly turnStarted: Promise<void>; /** Synchronous view of `turnStarted`, so a caller can skip building a bounded race when the start already arrived (an `agent_start` can precede the acknowledgement). */ readonly hasStarted: boolean; /** The caller's bound expired first: restores `runState` to its pre-prompt value without firing `onIdle`, exactly like a refused prompt — only if this receipt is still the last prompt sent on this client, the turn has not been observed, and `runState` is still the optimistic `"running"` (a socket close's `"unknown"` is never clobbered). Idempotent. */ abandonWait(): void; }
clientContract.internals: One slot, `pendingTurnStart`, holding the resolvers of the last prompt sent. `prompt()` arms the slot BEFORE `request("prompt", ...)` writes (so an `agent_start` racing the acknowledgement is not missed), keeps the existing optimistic `runState = "running"` and the existing refused-prompt restore, and on a rejection clears the slot if it still holds this prompt. `handleLine`'s `agent_start` branch and `getState()`'s `isStreaming === true` branch both set `runState = "running"` and resolve+clear the slot (`observeTurnStart()`). `agent_end`/`markIdle` are untouched. A refused prompt returns no receipt (it throws, as today).
clientContract.docUpdates: Rewrite the `prompt()` doc comment on `WorkerRpcClient`: the acknowledgement is not delivery; the receipt is how a caller learns the turn started.

errorClass.code: export class PromptNotStarted extends Error { constructor(readonly token: string, readonly boundMs: number, observation: string) { super(`worker ${token} acknowledged the prompt but started no turn within ${boundMs}ms (${observation})`); this.name = "PromptNotStarted"; } }

shape: const receipt = await client.prompt(pending.task);  // a rejection propagates exactly as today (refused-prompt path, untouched)

if (!started) { receipt.turnStarted.then(() => this.commitLateStart(token, issue, role, sessionId, pending)).catch((error) => console.error(`[legion] late-start commit for ${token} failed:`, error)); throw new PromptNotStarted(token, this.workerRpcTimeoutMs, observation); }
await this.commitPromptDelivery(token, issue, role, sessionId, pending, afterPrompt);
promptExistingWorker.awaitTurnStart: private async awaitTurnStart(client, receipt): Promise<{started: true} | {started: false; observation: string}>. If `receipt.hasStarted` return started (no timer built — keeps every existing test's `manualSleep.pending` untouched and makes the already-started case independent of microtask order). Else `const { timedOut, cancel } = boundedWait(this.workerRpcTimeoutMs, this.deps.sleep)` and race `receipt.turnStarted -> "started"`, `client.closed.then(() => "closed", () => "closed")`, `timedOut -> "timeout"`; always `cancel()` after the race. `"closed"` -> not started, observation `socket closed` (no get_state: the socket is gone; `onWorkerClientClosed` owns what happens next). `"timeout"` -> FIRST `receipt.abandonWait()` (silent restore, so the answer below is never an idle transition on a worker that was idle before the prompt), THEN one `client.getState(this.workerRpcTimeoutMs)`: `data.isStreaming === true` -> started (the client also resolved `turnStarted`); `false`/missing -> not started, observation `get_state: isStreaming=false`; rejection -> not started, observation `get_state failed: <message>`. The get_state is the spec's second signal and, for `/worker/ready` (pre-prompt `runState` is `"unknown"` — `clientFor` never asks get_state), the only thing that seeds the client idle so the queued retry is promotable at all.
promptExistingWorker.commitPromptDelivery: private async commitPromptDelivery(token, issue, role, sessionId, pending, afterPrompt?): the ONE commit block, shared by the normal path and the late path: (1) `if (pending.kind === "assignment") state.phases[issue] = { phase: role, sessionId }`; (2) on the claim: `delete pendingAssignment; promptFailures = 0`; (3) `afterPrompt?.()`; (4) `await this.workerAdmission.removeFromQueue(token)` (no-op when not queued); (5) the existing persist-with-one-retry from today's `promptExistingWorker` (log text unchanged except it now says the turn started). `promoteQueuedWorker`'s own post-prompt dequeue+persist (worker-admission.ts:627-633) is deleted; it keeps `this.launching.delete(token)`, the `worker-started` publish, and `return true`.
promptExistingWorker.commitLateStart: private async commitLateStart(token, issue, role, sessionId, pending): Promise<void>. Inside `this.workerAdmission.mutateClaim(token, ...)`: re-read the claim; return silently (no log) unless `claim` is a worker claim with `claim.sessionId === sessionId`, `claim.locator !== undefined`, `claim.pendingAssignment` equal BY VALUE to `pending` (`kind` and `task`; identity is not reliable across paths and a re-sent identical task is the same task), and the tree is not gone (`const treeKey = this.rootForIssue(issue); treeKey && !this.isTreeGone(treeKey, issue)`). Then one `console.info(`[legion] ${token} started its turn after the prompt wait expired; delivering the queued task now`)`, `await this.commitPromptDelivery(token, issue, role, sessionId, pending)`, `this.publishArchitect(treeKey, { type: "worker-started", issue, role })` (the architect was told `worker-queued` when the retry was queued). After the lock, if it committed, `this.workerAdmission.promoteWorkerQueue()` — the queue head moved, tokens behind it get their turn. A late start whose task was replaced or already delivered commits nothing: the newer task stays queued and is delivered once the worker is idle again.
promptExistingWorker.whyNoSecondPrompt: The receipt slot is per client and per last prompt; the late commit clears `pendingAssignment` and the queue entry, so no drain can prompt the task again. A retry already sent before the late start (the sweep ran first) arrives at OMP while it is streaming and is refused with `AgentBusyError` (a late `success:false` for an id our client already settled — ignored), so the worker never runs the task twice; the retry's own bound then expires, counts a failure, and the late commit that follows resets it.

sites.promoteQueuedWorker: worker-admission.ts `"prompt"` branch: the existing `catch` already does everything required for `PromptNotStarted` — `console.error(`[legion] failed to prompt queued worker ${token}:`, error)` (one line; the error message names the token and the observation), `this.launching.delete(token)`, count via the new `recordPromptFailure(token)` (extracted from lines 603-618: `promptFailures + 1`, `retireDeadClaim` at `MAX_LAUNCH_FAILURES` when a locator exists), `persist`, `return false`. Token never left the queue; `pendingAssignment` untouched (promptExistingWorker commits nothing before a started turn). Success path: `this.launching.delete(token)`, publish `worker-started`, `return true` (dequeue+persist now live in `commitPromptDelivery`).
sites.resumeOrQueueExisting: worker-admission.ts: wrap the admitted `promptExistingWorker` call: `catch (error) { if (!(error instanceof PromptNotStarted)) throw error; console.error(`[legion] ${token}: ${error.message}; queued for promotion`); await this.queueUnstartedPrompt(token, treeKey, issue, role, claim, pending); return { kind: "queued" }; } finally { this.release(token); onAdmissionEvent("reservation-released"); if (!notStarted) { this.promoteWorkerQueue(); onAdmissionEvent("queue-drain-triggered"); } }`. No drain trigger on the not-started path, for the same reason `promoteQueuedWorker`'s catch has none: it would re-peek this same head and re-prompt the same client at once, widening the window in which a merely slow worker receives the task twice; the retry is the next drain (an idle/dead event, the 60 s sweep, or the late start). `deliverToWorker` then answers `{status: "queued"}` to `spawn_worker`, and the architect receives `worker-queued` now and `worker-started` on the retry or the late start.
sites.workerReady: processes.ts: `try { await this.promptExistingWorker(client, token, issue, role, sessionId, pending, confirmBoot); } catch (error) { if (!(error instanceof PromptNotStarted)) throw error; confirmBoot(); this.cancelBootWatchdog(token, generation); console.error(`[legion] ${token}: ${error.message}; boot confirmed, task queued for promotion`); await this.workerAdmission.queueUnstartedPrompt(token, root, issue, role, claim, pending); return; }` where `confirmBoot` is today's `afterPrompt` body (`readyConfirmedAt = now(); delete launchFailures`). The boot DID succeed (registered, ready, socket answering); leaving it unconfirmed would strand the claim: `promoteQueuedWorker` stops on `readyConfirmedAt === undefined` and `spawnWorker` queues behind a boot that never confirms again. `queueUnstartedPrompt` persists, so the confirmation lands in the same save. No explicit drain trigger is needed here: the confirming `get_state` in `awaitTurnStart` seeds this fresh client from `"unknown"` to `"idle"`, whose `onIdle` (`clientFor`'s composed callback) triggers `promoteWorkerQueue()`, which queues behind this critical section and prompts the retry once — a genuine first idle observation, not a restore, so it is not the retry storm the silent-restore rule guards against.
workerAdmissionAdditions: `async removeFromQueue(token: string): Promise<void>` — public; splice under `withAdmissionLock`; used by `commitPromptDelivery`.

`private async recordPromptFailure(token: string): Promise<void>` — the body extracted from `promoteQueuedWorker`'s catch (count + retire at threshold via `retireDeadClaim`; caller holds the role lock; no persist).

`async queueUnstartedPrompt(token, treeKey, issue, role, claim, pending): Promise<void>` — public; `await withAdmissionLock(() => this.enqueueIdleWorker(token, claim, pending))` (writes `pendingAssignment`, pushes the token, locator untouched), `await this.recordPromptFailure(token)`, `await deps.persist()`, `deps.publishArchitect(treeKey, { type: "worker-queued", issue, role })`.

changes: `prompt()` returns a receipt: records the prompt, sets `runState = "running"` (as today), creates the receipt, and — when `client.turnStartsOnPrompt` (new field, default `true`) — starts it at once. Default true keeps every existing test's behaviour: a healthy worker's `agent_start` follows the acknowledgement.
`turnStartsOnPrompt: boolean` — a test sets it `false` to model an acknowledgement no turn follows.
`emitRunState("running")` also starts the pending receipt (models the `agent_start` frame); `emitRunState("idle")` unchanged.

The receipt's `abandonWait()` mirrors the real client: if not started and this is the last receipt and `runState === "running"`, restore the pre-prompt state silently (no `idleFireCount`, no callback).

`getStateImpl` stays a test-supplied function; tests that need the confirming get_state answer set it to `async () => ({ data: { isStreaming: false } })` (plus `emitRunState("idle")` when modelling the seed from `"unknown"`), exactly as `idleWorkerFixture` does today.

Three cases: (a) `fake-omp-rpc.ts` worker with a queued assignment: `reconnectWorkers()`, `enableLaunches()`, `reconcileWorkerAdmission()` -> queue empty, `phases[issue]` written, `promptFailures === 0`. steps.change: AGENTS.md: (1) row `POST /legion/v1/worker/ready` (line 19): 'cleared once sent' -> 'cleared once the worker's turn is observed to start'; add: an acknowledged prompt that starts no turn within `worker_rpc_timeout_seconds` still confirms the boot, leaves the task on the claim, queues the role for promotion, and counts against `promptFailures`. (2) row `POST /legion/v1/worker/spawn` (line 20): `resumed` means the live worker's turn started; an acknowledgement no turn follows answers `queued` with the task queued for promotion. (3) bullet 64 (`spawn_worker always resumes the same agent`): same qualifier on 'prompted directly over its socket (`resumed`)'. (4) bullets 66-67: rewrite 67 as the delivery definition — a prompt to a live worker (queue promotion, `spawn_worker`'s direct prompt, `/worker/ready`'s delivery) is delivered only when its turn is observed to start (`agent_start`, or `get_state` with `isStreaming: true`) within `worker_rpc_timeout_seconds` of the acknowledgement; the shim's `{success:true}` is not delivery (OMP acknowledges before the turn starts and can accept a prompt that starts none); only a started turn removes the queue entry, clears `pendingAssignment`, writes `phases[issue]`, resets `promptFailures`; an acknowledgement no turn follows is a prompt failure exactly like a refusal (silent run-state restore, `promptFailures` +1, one log line naming the token, entry stays queued — the two direct paths queue it — retried on the next drain, retired at `MAX_LAUNCH_FAILURES` so the assignment relaunches cold with `--resume`); a turn that starts after the bound is the same task and is committed at that moment (queue entry removed, pending cleared, phase written, failures reset, `worker-started` published) with no second prompt — a retry already in flight is refused by OMP (`AgentBusyError`); a restart mid-promotion leaves the entry queued with its task and boot's `reconcileWorkerAdmission` re-prompts it once `reconnectWorkers` seeds the client idle. legion-state.ts:144-149 `promptFailures` doc: 'Consecutive prompt() rejections' -> 'Consecutive failed prompt attempts (a refusal, or an acknowledgement no turn followed within the bound)'. skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:265 `worker-queued` row: also sent when a live worker acknowledged the task without starting a turn and the daemon is retrying; the instruction stays 'wait for worker-started'. tools.ts:75-80 description: `resumed` = prompted and its turn started; `queued` = at cap OR acknowledged without a turn (daemon retries).

proof.unit: `cd packages/daemon && bun test` — the whole daemon suite. Regression locks only; not acceptance evidence.
proof.integration: real-prompt-delivery-e2e.test.ts on this box: real tmux server (`tmux -L legion-<project>`), real `legion worker-shim` subprocess, real unix socket and `WorkerRpcClient`, real `TmuxRuntime` probe/stop (the retire at threshold really kills the pane), fixture OMP stand-ins for the three worker behaviours. This is the 'scratch daemon with a real tmux server' half of the spec's Testing section; it cannot run a real OMP because the boot handshake (`/worker/started`, `/worker/ready`) is performed by the pi-envoy plugin inside OMP.

rig.surface: The Legion smoke rig (`scripts/smoke/up.sh`, `SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=envoy`) — real daemon, real tmux, real OMP workers with the real plugin tree. Owner: the tester (the implementer runs it too when the rig is already up). Record the `E2E` line with the head SHA, the state.json snapshots, the daemon log lines, and the architect pane's `worker-queued`/`worker-started` deliveries.
rig.setup: After `up.sh`, set `worker_cap: 1` in `${SMOKE_DIR}/legion.yaml` (the rig writes 6) and restart the daemon so the cap is one; let the root tree run until one phase worker is finished and idle-live (e.g. the planner after `phase-complete`) while another is running (cap full). Read `<state_dir>/state.json` (the API and `legion state` redact `workerAdmission.queue` and `promptFailures`).
rig.positive: Have the architect `spawn_worker` the idle-live role again with a small task (attach: `tmux -L legion-<project> attach -t legion-<project>`; the architect pane accepts a typed instruction). Expect: `spawn_worker` answers `queued`, state.json shows the token on `workerAdmission.queue` with `pendingAssignment`; when the running worker finishes, the promotion prompts the idle worker and state.json shows `phases[<issue>]` for that role and the queue empty only once that worker's pane shows the new turn (its OMP transcript gains the user message and an assistant turn begins); the daemon log has no `acknowledged the prompt but started no turn` line for it; the architect pane receives `worker-started`.
rig.negativeControl: The spec's fake shim, on the real daemon: (1) pick the idle-live worker with a queued task (as above, before the running worker finishes); (2) stop the daemon (`legion stop <team>`); (3) in the rig's private tmux session open a pane running the ack-only stand-in behind a real shim: `bun packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts worker-shim --socket <new sock> -- bun packages/daemon/src/cli/__tests__/fixtures/delayed-start-omp-rpc.ts` (no delay env => never starts a turn), and `tmux kill-pane` the real idle worker's pane; (4) edit state.json: on that claim's `locator` set `socketPath` to the new socket and `tmuxWindowId`/`tmuxPaneId`/`panePid`/`paneStartTicks` to the stand-in pane's values (`tmux -L legion-<project> list-panes -a -F '#{window_id} #{pane_id} #{pane_pid}'`, start ticks from `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22), keep `ompSessionFile` (it is the real agent's transcript, which the relaunch resumes); (5) start the daemon. Expect, in order: boot's `reconnectWorkers` connects to the stand-in and `reconcileWorkerAdmission` promotes the queued entry (acceptance 4 on the real surface); within `worker_rpc_timeout_seconds` the log prints `[legion] failed to prompt queued worker <token>: worker <token> acknowledged the prompt but started no turn within <N>ms (get_state: isStreaming=false)` and state.json shows `promptFailures: 1` with the queue and `pendingAssignment` intact; the next two sweeps (60 s each) repeat it to 3; at 3 the stand-in pane is killed (gone from `list-panes`), the claim's locator is cleared with `resumeSessionFile` set, the queue still holds the token; the following drain relaunches the real worker cold — a new pane whose command carries `--resume=<session file>` — it boots, `/worker/ready` delivers the task, the worker runs it, and the architect pane receives `worker-started`. If the daemon skipped the stand-in's kill because the pane identity did not verify, the log names `not-recorded-process`: re-check step (4).

outOfScope: Using OMP's `prompt_result {agentInvoked:false}` frame as an early definitive negative: it would shorten the wait from the bound to milliseconds on the one code path that emits it, but the spec names `agent_start`/`get_state` as the signals, the bound already covers it, and every fake client in the suite would need a second negative path. Note it in the retro if the 5 s bound proves costly.

Exposing `promptFailures` and `workerAdmission.queue` in `GET /legion/v1/state` / `legion state`: would let an architect see a stuck promotion without reading state.json, but the state response is a strict `LegionDaemonApi` shape — any field is a contract bump plus a lockstep plugin release. Not needed for this fix.
Probing a queue head whose client is `runState: "unknown"` from the drain (today `promoteQueuedWorker` stops on it): pre-existing; see concerns for the one narrow way this change can reach it.

Writing `pendingAssignment` + queueing BEFORE the direct `resumed` prompt so a crash during the bounded wait is redriven at boot like a promotion: a redesign of `resumeOrQueueExisting`'s contract (`queued` vs `resumed` publications); today's direct path already loses the task on a crash between acknowledgement and persist, and the spec scopes constraint 4 to the not-started outcome.
concerns: Turn attribution is by order, not by id: the first `agent_start` after a prompt is taken to be that prompt's turn (spec: the daemon serializes prompts per role and is the only prompter of an idle worker). An Envoy delivery to the worker (another role's question, a targeted Dispatch message) can start a turn in that window and be mistaken for the delivery; the task is then still in OMP's queue (or refused) and the daemon believes it delivered. Accepted by the spec; the retro should watch for it.

Double-prompt window for a merely slow worker: if the turn starts after the bound AND a retry was already sent by the next drain, OMP refuses the retry with `AgentBusyError` once it is streaming — but if the retry lands while OMP is still in `session.prompt`'s pre-turn awaits, OMP has two prompts in flight and the second becomes a follow-up or an error; the daemon cannot tell. Mitigations built in: no immediate re-drain on the two silent paths, the late commit clears the queue entry the moment the turn is seen. If a deployment's `worker_rpc_timeout_seconds` (5) is too tight for its host, raise it there.

`/worker/ready` residual: a ready-time prompt that starts no turn AND whose confirming `get_state` also fails leaves the fresh client at `runState: "unknown"`; the task is queued and counted, but `promoteQueuedWorker` stops on an unknown head until the next `spawn_worker` for that role probes it (`get_state` seeds it) or a restart's `reconnectWorkers` does. Logged (`get_state failed: ...`); rare (the shim answered the prompt but not a `get_state` within the bound). Listed in outOfScope as the general drain-probe fix.

A restart between an observed start and its persisted commit (or between a late `agent_start` and `commitLateStart`'s save) leaves the entry queued while the worker is running the task: boot's drain stops on the running client and re-prompts once it is idle — the task runs twice. Pre-existing semantics for any restart mid-commit; the alternative (trusting an unobserved turn) is the bug being fixed.

Test churn is mechanical but wide: five inline `WorkerRpcClient` literals, three `client.prompt` overrides, two `worker-rpc.test.ts` assertions, and the fake client's default must keep starting the turn on prompt or ~40 existing tests silently turn into not-started paths that wait on a real 5 s timer.

The bounded wait holds the role lock (`mutateClaim(token)`) for up to 2×`worker_rpc_timeout_seconds` on a failing prompt; `spawn_worker` answers within that time and `drainWorkerQueue` is sequential per pass. Acceptable at the deployment's cap sizes; not a behaviour change on the happy path (agent_start arrives within milliseconds).
